name: 180 Degrees Consulting
description:
180 Degrees Consulting at Iowa State University is a student-led organization that works on real-world consulting cases with companies, with a strong focus on socially conscious organizations and small businesses. As a chapter of the world’s largest university-based consultancy, we equip students with hands-on experience in problem-solving, strategy, and analytics through live client engagements.
In addition to client work, we actively prepare for and participate in case competitions and host weekly case practice sessions to help members build structured thinking, consulting skills, and interview readiness while creating meaningful impact in the community.
allowedMembers: Membership is open to all Iowa State University students with a GPA of 2.0 or higher. We welcome students from all majors who are passionate about creating social impact or developing real-world problem-solving skills.
elections: Executive board elections are held annually toward the end of the spring semester.
meetings: Weekly meetings are held every Monday from 5:30-6:30 PM in Gerdin. These sessions include project updates, training, case preparation and team collaboration. All members are expected to attend and actively participate.
activities: Our core activities include consulting projects for nonprofits and socially conscious organizations, giving members hands-on experience in solving real-world problems. We also participate in and host case competitions to help students sharpen their analytical and strategic thinking skills.

name: AA Stand Up Comedy Club
description:
The Stand Up Comedy Club is a group dedicated to offering opportunities for students to perform original stand up comedy routines in front of live audiences. The group is composed of students of varying experience levels who work together to write, edit, and perform original stand up comedy routines. Occasionally the club might host a traveling comedian who can share advice with members and grow the network of comedians around the country. Regularly, club members can be seen at local bars, comedy clubs, theaters, and campus events.

To book the Stand Up Comedy Club for a show, where we typically do showcase style shows where a group of comedians does about 10 minutes or less each, please contact a club officer from our directory or email the club in general at: isusucc@gmail.com
membershipQualifications: a heartbeat, half a brain, and a whole lot of courage. Being able to suppress feelings of sadness is also a plus
elections: Majority vote at a general meeting. Elections will be scheduled at least two weeks in advance so that members are aware of the upcoming elections
meetings: 7-8:00 PM every Monday in Curtiss 0108
activities:
General meetings: Mondays from 6:30-8:00 pm in Curtiss 0108. Meetings will consist of group writing, editing, presentation, and possible road trips to open mics in the area to rigorously train and master our craft.

For more information about our club/club meetings, you may subscribe to receive our weekly emails through the "subscribe" button, or you may reach out to any of the club officers via email.
specialEvents:
The club will occasionally take trips to local venues, either on-campus or in the Ames area.

Comedy venues in the Des Moines area are also a possibility.

The Club will host at least one show per semester to raise funds and showcase our performers.

name: Advertising Club
description: The Advertising Club at Iowa State focuses on networking with communications professionals and learning about a career in advertising and marketing. We meet every other Wednesday in Hamilton Hall with guest speakers and local projects! Each spring, we take a trip to meet with and tour advertising agencies to learn about the industry and day-to-day expectations. In the past, we have visited Kansas City, Austin, Chicago, and Denver!
membershipQualifications: None
allowedMembers: Anyone displaying interest in advertising and the industry regardless of major
elections: End of the Fall semester
meetings: Meet every other Wednesday in 0163 Hamilton Hall at 7:30pm.
activities: In the main meetings we collaborate on real life projects and create advertisements for business and other clubs. On top of that, we bring in professional speakers in the industry and take tours of local ad agencies in Des Moines. Along with tours, we create networking sessions with advertising and marketing professionals, including resume, portfolio and professional development workshops. It's the perfect head start into any creative career.
specialEvents: Ad Club has an annual Spring Trip where we take students to tour advertising agencies in cities such as: Chicago, Minneapolis, Kansas City, Denver, and Dallas. The goal is to experience agency cultures and build connections. It's an awesome opportunity to establish networking skills and be face to face with potential employers. However, the trip isn't just for business. We do find time to do fun activities and explore the city!

name: Aeronautical Innovative Research
description:
Dedicated to pushing the boundaries of aeronautical science and engineering, our club is committed to creating an innovative and educational environment for all club participants. With a primary focus on aerodynamics, controls, rocketry, aircraft systems, computational fluid dynamics, aerostructures, and engineering, we aim to drive impactful research that advances the field of aerospace.
Through collaborative projects and hands-on experimentation, members of the club will have the opportunity to engage in cutting-edge research efforts. Our goal is to not only expand the knowledge and understanding of our members, but also to contribute to real-world solutions that address known and unknown challenges in the world of aeronautics.
elections: Elections for ALL leadership rolls are to occur in the month of February at the beginning of every spring semester.
meetings: Weekly club addresses are to occur every Thursday unless otherwise specified. There will also be a club work sessions every Sunday unless otherwise specified.
activities: There are general meetings for all club members that occur weekly on Wednesdays at 7:00 pm CST in Howe Hall, room 1252 (subject to change on a semester basis). This meeting addresses club news, weekly workflow updates, and where efforts need to be prioritized. There are also individual sub-team work sessions organized by sub-team leads. This meeting is mandatory for all sub-teams.

name: Africa Learning and Evolving Community
description: The Africa Learning & Evolving Community (AFLEC) at Iowa State University is a professional network committed to promoting academic excellence, cross-cultural engagement, and leadership growth among scholars from Africa and those with a scholarly focus on African issues.
elections: Annually
meetings: At least once Monthly
activities: General Body Meetings | Executive Board Meetings | Special Events Planning Sessions | Professional Development Workshops | Mentorship Program Match-Up | Cultural & Social Events | Volunteer Opportunities | Industry & Corporate Tours | Planning & Strategy Retreats
specialEvents: Afrisolve Idea Hackathon | Industrial & Cultural Trips | World Food Prize Day | AFLEC Get Fit | Welcome Orientation
homeText:
Empowering African Scholars at Iowa State University

The Africa Learning & Evolving Community (AFLEC) Student Organization at Iowa State University is a professional network dedicated to fostering academic excellence, cultural exchange, and leadership development among African and Africa-engaged scholars. Through a robust calendar of seminars, workshops, and cultural celebrations, AFLEC connects members with distinguished faculty, industry mentors, and alumni to advance research collaboration and career readiness.

Our mission is to:

- Empower students and early-career professionals by providing tailored training in grant writing, presentation skills, and professional branding.

- Celebrate the diversity of African cultures via heritage nights, art exhibitions, and community service initiatives.

- Cultivate a supportive environment where peer-to-peer mentoring and interdisciplinary dialogue thrive.

By bridging Iowa State’s world-class resources with Africa’s rich intellectual traditions, AFLEC prepares its members to become tomorrow’s global leaders, innovators in research, advocates for social impact, and ambassadors of intercultural understanding.

name: AI & ML Club
description: The AI & ML Club at Iowa State University fosters a community for students passionate about Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, and Machine Learning. Our mission is to unite like-minded individuals to collaborate, compete, and develop professionally within a supportive and dynamic environment. We provide hands-on projects in AI, ML, and emerging fields such as Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), AI Agents, and MCP servers, equipping members with practical skills and real-world experience. Join us to explore innovative solutions, construct impactful projects, and become an integral part of a forward-thinking community committed to shaping the future of intelligent systems.
membershipQualifications: Besides being a full-time or half-time student at Iowa State University in a relevant major, candidates must submit a join request, explain their interest in about 35–40 words describing why they want to join the club and what they hope to achieve, and agree to regularly attend meetings and contribute to projects.

By joining, you commit to attending all or most meetings, since we’ll be working on projects where teams depend on members who can actively contribute and follow through.
elections: No elections will be held until the current member graduates. Once eligible, elections for officer positions will be held annually, typically during the first meeting of each Fall semester. A majority vote from the general membership is required to elect officers. If no candidate secures a majority, a run-off election will be conducted between the top two candidates with the most votes. homeText:
The AI & ML Club at Iowa State University is a community for students who want to go beyond learning AI and actually build it.

We bring together curious, driven minds interested in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Computer Science to explore ideas, experiment with new technologies, and create systems that matter. Our culture is rooted in collaboration, creativity, and healthy competition, pushing members to think deeper, move faster, and grow together.

Our focus is practical and forward-looking . Members work hands-on with modern AI paradigms including Machine Learning, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, AI Agents, and MCP-based systems. By operating at the intersection of these technologies, we prepare students to solve complex real-world problems and design intelligent systems that are scalable, explainable, and future-ready.

Through project-based learning, technical workshops, and curated events, members gain real experience building AI-driven applications, deploying multi-agent architectures, and working with cutting-edge frameworks used in industry and research. Every initiative is designed to strengthen technical depth while encouraging exploration of what’s next in AI.

Join the AI & ML Club to sharpen your skills, collaborate with ambitious peers, and help shape the future of intelligent systems.

For Spring 2026, the AI & ML Club meets every Thursday at 5:30 PM in Gerdin 1464.

The purpose of the Algorithmic Trading Club (ATC) at Iowa State University is to provide a collaborative environment where students can explore, develop, and apply algorithmic trading strategies. The club aims to:

homeText:
What is Alpha Omega?

Alpha Omega Campus Ministry is a group of Bible-believers at Iowa State. We seek to navigate students through their faith while at college by enriching them in the gospel message. We are a diverse group of students seeking to enrich our spiritual lives and glorify God through all we do. One of the hardest things to do in college is maintain a strong walk with God - we become distracted so easily by all college has to offer. Through our weekly events such as Bible Talks, Devotionals, and meeting for church on Sundays, we aim to build students up and build their relationship with God. Our ministry also seeks to build deep, lasting friendships which will not only guide them through college, but for life.

What Do We Do?

Bible Talks

6:30PM Tuesdays

Memorial Union Pine Room

A short group Bible lesson in which we read and discuss scripture and how it can apply to our daily life and strengthen our walk with God.

Devotionals

7PM Thursdays

0268 Carver Hall

Each Thursday we host a devotional which includes a Biblical message, songs, and time for fellowship with each other.

Personal Bible Studies

Whenever

Wherever

If you are interested in studying the Bible, we are always looking to connect with you! We set up times that fit your schedule to provide and personalize a study plan to fit your needs.

Events & Retreats

Volleyball

Join us for volleyball every Tuesday (weather permitting) on Central Campus near the Campanile.

If it is rainy, snowy, or there is other midwestern weather, we play pool or bowling inside of the Memorial Union!

Check out our social media for updates!

Midwest Autumn Campus (MAC) Retreat

Each year, our fellowship of campus ministries throughout the Midwest gather at Lake Geneva, Wisconsin for a weekend retreat. The retreat is a great opportunity to connect with other Christian college students in the Midwest, where there are opportunities to worship, go to breakout lessons, play games (including a volleyball tournament), and have bonfires.

This past year's MAC theme was ALTAR! Join us next fall for the MAC!

International Campus Ministry Conference (ICMC)

During the summer, our fellowship of campus ministries meets for a large-scale conference where we sing worship, attend sessions to growth in our faith, and meet thousands of other campus-aged Christians.

Next year's ICMC will be held in Milwaukee, WI from July 30 - August 2nd, 2026. Here is the website that will contain more info as it is released. The theme is Proclaim, so get ready to praise God with us and thousands of others from all over the world!

homeText:
Welcome to APO!

Alpha Phi Omega is a national co-ed fraternity, not associated with Greek life on campus. With more than 500,000 members on over 375 campuses across the United States, APO continues to provide more service on more campuses than any other collegiate service organization. Founded on the principles of the Boy Scouts of America, we focus on three cardinal principles: to develop Leadership, to promote Friendship, and to provide Service to humanity. We provide our members the opportunity to develop leadership skills and volunteer on and off-campus, all while having fun and making life-long friendships.

Leadership

As a national organization, APO strives to develop our members as leaders through service to others. This approach builds the leadership skills of our members while fulfilling a need on campuses and in communities, therefore leaving a lasting impact on our nation. Our members have the opportunity to serve as a member of the executive board, plan and host any number of volunteer and social events, and participate in a variety of developmental programs. We also encourage leadership outside of APO, whether that be in another club or any other area of your life!

Friendship

Friendship is extremely important to us here at Iowa State, as many see our chapter as a second family. College can be stressful; that's why we are here for you! Our club is open to everybody, no matter your major, classification, or experience with volunteering. We host a wide variety of fellowship events, from outdoor hikes and Bob Ross nights, to video games and holiday parties. You will be sure to find something you enjoy!

Service

Service is the main goal of APO, and we look to impact the community in the most positive ways possible. With our foundation in Scouts, we are proud to host our annual Merit Badge University every spring, an opportunity for scouts across the United States to visit Iowa State University and earn merit badges. Although this is a very important part of what we do, there are hundreds of service opportunities available that can fit in with your busy schedule!

name: Alpha Phi Sigma
description:
Alpha Phi Sigma, the National Criminal Justice Honor Society, recognizes the academic excellence of undergraduate, graduate, and Juris Doctorate students. Alpha Phi Sigma (APS) is the only honor society for students of the criminal justice sciences recognized by the Association of College Honor Societies. The Honor Society is open to those with a declared major, minor or equivalent in a Criminal Justice or related field leading to a Bachelor's degree, Master's degree, or Doctoral degree. Membership Alpha Phi Sigma signifies your dedication to academic excellence, leadership, service and unity, and allows you to join the ranks of thousands of other Alpha Phi Sigma members and alumni across the world who make a positive difference each day in their professions and communities. The mission of Alpha Phi Sigma is to promote analytical
thinking, rigorous scholarship, and lifelong learning; to keep abreast of the advances in scientific research; to elevate the ethical standards of the criminal justice professions; and to sustain in the public mind the benefits and necessity of education and professional training.
membershipQualifications:
1. Baccalaureate students shall be enrolled at the time of application at Iowa State University, have declared a major, minor or equivalent in the criminal justice or related field, have completed three full time semesters or its equivalent, have a minimum GPA of 3.2 on a 4.0 scale, with a minimum GPA of 3.2 in courses in criminal justice related fields and rank in the top 35% of their class. A minimum of four courses of the above course work shall be in the criminal justice field.

2. Masters students shall be enrolled at the time of application in a Masters program in the Criminal Justice field at Iowa State University, have completed four courses, and have a minimum GPA of 3.4 on a 4.0 scale. Up to three undergraduate courses in Criminal Justice may be used to satisfy the four-course requirement. These courses must equate to a 3.4 GPA or higher, and the cumulative undergraduate degree program GPA is a 3.2 or higher. In addition, all Masters level coursework must equate to a 3.4 GPA or higher at the institution in which the student is enrolled.

3. Doctoral Students shall be enrolled at the time of application in a Ph.D. program in the Criminal Justice/ related field at Iowa State University, have completed four courses, have a minimum GPA of 3.6 on a 4.0 scale. Up to three Masters courses in Criminal Justice may be used to satisfy the four-course requirement. These courses must equate to a 3.6 GPA or higher, and the cumulative Master’s degree program GPA is a 3.4 or higher. In addition, any Ph.D. level coursework must equate to a 3.6 GPA or higher at the institution in which the student is enrolled.

4. Students enrolled in law school, must have completed their first academic semester with a grade point average of 2.5 or higher on a 4.0 scale.

5. Transfer Members. Any Alpha Phi Sigma member who transfers to another college or university shall be accepted into the local chapter at Iowa State University and shall pay the local chapter fee, if any. After one term, the member shall be subject to all rules, regulations, and requirements of the Pi Epsilon Lambda chapter. Headquarters will not issue a new certificate of membership unless specifically requested by the chapter advisor and paid for by the member.

B. Faculty Members Faculty and administration involvement is recognized and encouraged. Candidates for membership must be full-time faculty or administrators in a criminal justice related field unless the college primarily uses Adjunct faculty. They must have completed a minimum of one-year full-time teaching/administrative duties at Iowa State University where they are inducted and elected by majority vote during a regular meeting. Membership applications shall be approved and signed by the chapter advisor, submitted to and accepted by Headquarters.

C. Honorary Members. Honorary membership recognizes community people who have made distinctive scholarly and research contributions to the criminal justice field or who have provided outstanding support for the Pi Epsilon Lambda chapter. Honorary Members may not be students. The Chapter Advisor shall approve nominations. Honorary Members must be elected by a 2/3 vote of the chapter. The Pi Epsilon Lambda chapter may elect Honorary Members during a regular meeting. Membership applications shall be approved and signed by the chapter advisor, submitted to, and accepted by Headquarters.

D. Professional Members. Includes College/University graduates not previously initiated into Alpha Phi Sigma.

1. Eligibility: Professionals shall have made a distinctive contribution to the profession; shall have earned one or more degrees in criminal justice or related field from a regionally accredited institution; working in the profession as a criminal justice practitioner for a minimum of two (2) years; shall have a minimum cumulative 3.2 GPA on a 4.0 scale as undergraduate student or minimum cumulative 3.4 GPA on a 4.0 scale as graduate student. Academic transcript and personal resume must accompany the application. Membership application packet must be submitted to Headquarters and approved by the Executive Director.

2. Professional members have the option of being part of the Alumni Association, Alumni Circle, active, or golden.

E. Alumni Members. Pi Epsilon Lambda Collegiate members in good standing at the time of graduation from Iowa State University are alumni members.

F. Alumni Association Members. Alumni Association Members are Alpha Phi Sigma alumni members that have applied for membership in the Alumni Association. There are two categories of Alumni, active and golden.

1. Active – Alumni shall apply for membership and contribute an annual fee to the Alumni Association.

2. Golden– Alumni shall apply for membership and contribute a one-time fee to Headquarters.

a. Faculty members teaching in the field of Criminal Justice and are a chapter
advisor for a minimum of five years, may apply for Golden Alumni Membership.

b. Professional members have the option of being part of the Alumni association, alumni circle, active, or golden.

Section 3. Additional Qualifications. Membership in the Society is open to qualified candidates including persons with disability, without regard to age, color, gender, national origin, race, religion, and/or sexual orientation.

Section 4. Privileges of Membership. Active, Alumni Members, and Golden Members shall have the right to vote, hold appropriate office, be elected or appointed to committees of the Pi Epsilon Lambda chapter provided other uniform criteria are met, and shall have such other privileges as the Executive Advisory Board shall determine. Honorary members and Professional members shall have all the privileges of active members except the right to vote, hold office or serve on committees, unless allowed at the chapter level.

a. Faculty members (Other than the Chapter Advisor), Honorary members, Professional members, and Alumni members shall have all the privileges of active members except the right to vote, and hold office.

elections:
Section 4. Elections.
a. General elections will be held to replace officers whose terms are due to expire.

b. Special elections shall be held when an office is vacated before a term has expired.

c. Nomination of candidates: A candidate for office must be nominated by a voting member during the first meeting in September, in the case of general elections or during the meeting immediately prior to special elections.

d. Time of Elections: General elections shall be held during the first meeting in September and special elections shall be held as necessary.

e. Form of Vote: All elections shall be by secret ballot.
meetings:
Section 1: Quorum. To conduct business, a simple majority of the total voting membership must be present at the meeting. A simple majority of the total voting membership must be present for all elections.

Section 2: Voting Percentages. Motions dealing with amendments and the removal of officers will require a simple majority vote of the total voting membership. All other motions will require a simple majority vote of the quorum to pass.

Section 3: Parliamentary Authority. The bylaws of Pi Epsilon Lambda shall be the supreme authority in parliamentary procedure at all meetings. Robert’s Rules of Order shall be the procedure used to conduct meetings except where it conflicts with these bylaws.

Section 4: Frequency of Meetings. Pi Epsilon Lambda shall meet monthly during the semester. The Advisor, President or a 2/3 majority of the total voting membership may call emergency meetings. Written and/or verbal notice of Pi Epsilon Lambda meetings shall be given to all members at least 7 days prior to such meetings. Written and/or verbal notice of special or emergency meetings shall be given to all members at least 3 days in advance.

Alpha Pi Mu is an invite-only industrial engineering honors society that recognizes top junior and senior industrial engineering students for their academic achievements, increases professional development among members, and promotes networking among faculty, graduate, and undergraduate students through social, professional, and service opportunities. What truly sets Alpha Sigma Phi, Phi Chapter apart from other organizations is its brotherhood. Found within the chapter is a strong devotion to the ideology of Alpha Sigma Phi and the characteristics of brotherhood. Throughout the semester the organization hosts seminars for hands-on experience with joint injections, laparoscopy, equine dentistry, etc. Members will be connected with the National AAEP and introduced to current ethical issues, pharmaceutical products, medical procedures, and professional considerations of interest, such as residency programs. Additionally, members will be able to go to National AAEP Conventions, visit various equine clinics, and learn about equine cases through ‘Equine Rounds’ with the clinicians from the medical center. Students interested in equine medicine and those that have a recreational interest in the equine species are encouraged to join.
membershipQualifications:
Members- none
Executive team- horse experience
elections: Elections are held in the spring semester over an internet poll.
meetings:
Members- none mandatory
Executive team- only miss one executive meeting per semester is preferred
activities: We meet once to twice per month for lunch meetings as a club. The executive team meets twice per month. During lunch meetings, students receive lunch and listen to speakers who are doctors either from our faculty or brought to the school from elsewhere. Topics include equine lameness, dentals, dystocia, managing an equine practice, dermatology, opthomology, farrier work, and many others.
specialEvents: AAEP is one of the busiest clubs at ISU Vet Med. We have 3 wetlabs per semester including horse handling, castration, radiology, farrier, dental, opthomology, volunteerism at one of the local horse riding camps, chiropractic, and many others. We also attend national convention and Rolex as a group which really makes those events fun.

American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics at Iowa State University

- Our mission is to advance the state of aerospace science, engineering, technology, operations, and policy at Iowa State University.

- We address the professional needs and interests of the past, current, and future aerospace workforce.

- AIAA at ISU is open to all engineering majors who may be interested in aerospace or aeronautics.

Click Here to learn more about us!

American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics

Iowa State University Student Branch

AIAA is the world's largest technical society dedicated to the global aerospace profession. AIAA has nearly 30,000 members from 91 countries, and 95 corporate members.

Our Purpose

AIAA offers students opportunities to identify and build toward career goals, attend guest speaker events, and network with colleagues of different age groups. We host meetings for career fair prep, resume building, interview best practices, LinkedIn seminars, barbeques, and we host 4-6 speakers a semester.

"One of my favorite things about AIAA is that our guest speaker events aren't just seminars our members sit through. We get to connect with speakers and even participate in the meetings themselves because our guests are excited to come and talk with interested and hungry future engineers"

- Daniel Sisco senior at Iowa State University

homeText:
Welcome to the American Nuclear Society Student Section website! We're an organization dedicated to connecting ISU students with professionals from all over the nuclear industry. Whether you're considering a career in the nuclear sector or just want to learn more about nuclear technology, you've come to the right place!

Each semester, we invite several speakers to give presentations about their role in the nuclear field. These presentations are free and open to the public, so we'd love to see you there! Check our calendar below for detailed information about each event!

We don't just have speakers come to see us; we occasionally hit the road to see what life is like working in the nuclear sector! We previously toured the Quad Cities Generating Station in Spring 2026, and future trips may include other generating facilities, National Labs, and more!

Questions? Reach out to one of the officers, and we'll be happy to answer them!

homeText:
The Iowa State University chapter of ASABE (American Society of Agricultural and Biological Systems Engineers) gives students opportunities to connect with industry professionals, explore careers, and get involved outside of the classroom.

Throughout the year, we host meetings featuring guest speakers from agricultural and biological systems engineering industries who share what their companies do, career opportunities, internships, and their experiences in the field. We also take trips and tours of facilities, participate in hands-on and professional experiences, and host social activities that allow members to connect with one another.

Our goal is to help students learn more about the many career paths within agricultural and biological systems engineering while building connections, gaining experience, and having fun along the way.

Whether you’re looking to learn more about the industry, explore internship opportunities, meet other students, or simply get involved, ASABE is a great place to start!

name: American Society of Mechanical Engineers
description:
Since its founding in 1880 the American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) strives to be the premier worldwide organization for promoting the art, science, and practice of mechanical engineering. Today ASME is comprised of over 125,000 members from around the globe, making up over 400 sections and student sections. The society serves engineering professionals, students, and educators alike.

The section of ASME at Iowa State University is completely student run. It provides student members with the opportunities to grow beyond the classroom. The section has many activities throughout the academic year that are geared towards extended learning. These include industry sponsored meetings, professional discussions, and design competitions.

Company representatives frequently participate in our regularly scheduled events to meet ASME members, and learn more about member’s participation in design competitions, student professional development conferences and community outreach.
membershipQualifications:
It is not required, but we highly encourage our members to register with ASME International at:
https://www.asme.org/professional-membership
elections: Elections are held at the end of each spring semester to fill open and new positions.
meetings: Locations and times will be sent out in update emails each week. Be sure to subscribe to our email list to stay updated.
activities:
Typical group meetings include a presenter from a company of interest. These company representatives speak on a range of topics including details about their company and position, engineering skills, and career development. We encourage our members to network with these representatives after our meetings conclude.

Cabinet meetings are typically held before general meetings from 5pm-6pm. These are open to members interested in becoming more involved with the club.
specialEvents: Depending on Event, email officer's for clarification

name: American Veterinary Society of Animal Behavior - Student Chapter
description: Educate students and the public about the importance of animal behavior as it pertains to Vet Med livestock production, safety, and pet behavior problems and or training.
membershipQualifications: Admission to ISU CVM as a candidate for the DVM degree. Officers must maintain a 2.5 GPA
membershipRestrictions: Open to current vet med students only.
elections: Elections take place at the end of the school year in the spring. Any unfilled positions will be re-opened for election at the start of the next school year in the fall.
meetings: Scheduled several times a year.
activities: Behavior Club tries to bring speakers in to talk about animal behavior in a way that will help you as a veterinary student. This includes how to better restrain fractious cats in your clinic, and how to solve some cat behavior problems like urinating outside of the litter box, which may be helpful for your personal knowledge or for educating your clients. We offer a clicker training class for members to learn the basics of clicker training and we have also had speakers in the past talk about the many different activities an owner can do with their dogs. Some of the most popular speakers we have are those who teach us about how they work with and train the many different animals in a zoo.
specialEvents: This fall Behavior Club members traveled to the Blank Park Zoo to get up close and personal during the training sessions. Students were able to see Rhino training, Aldabra Tortoise training, and Seal and Sea Lion training. We were able to talk with the trainers about the challenges that go along with training these unique animals and how they have overcome these obstacles. We hope to make this an annual event.
homeText: Educate students and the public about the importance of animal behavior as it pertains to Vet Med livestock production, safety, and pet behavior problems and or training.

name: Antique Tractor Club
description: The Antique Tractor Club at Iowa State University is a club designed for students with an interest in antique farm equipment. The club works on repairing & restoring one antique tractor per year. The club typically meets twice a week for two hours in the Sukup Hall shop, or off campus and works on the tractor restoration project. Several trips to antique tractor collections are taken during the year. Every month we have one classroom meeting where discussion of events and business take place.

specialEvents: The club takes one fall trip where we tour a tractor collection or an Ag based business that pertains to most of our majors. We also take a spring trip at the end of the year where we usually leave on a Friday and come back on a Saturday. We have been to several places such as the Keller Collection in Wisconsin, the Jon Kinzenbaw Collection, Farmall Land, the Charles City Museum, and the University of Nebraska-Lincoln.

name: Asian Student Union
description: The Asian Student Union (ASU) at Iowa State University is dedicated to building an inclusive, welcoming community where students of all backgrounds can connect, grow, and celebrate Asian cultures. Our mission is to foster appreciation and awareness of the diverse traditions, customs, and experiences across Asia while creating a supportive space for friendship, leadership, and personal growth. Through cultural showcases like InnovAsian, social gatherings, professional networking, and collaborative events, we strive to highlight the beauty of our differences and bring people together. Whether Asian or non-Asian, every student is encouraged to join with an open mind, make meaningful connections, and feel at home within our community.
membershipQualifications: Anyone is able to join ASU! Come attend meetings, hang out with members, get involved at events, and help spread the word about Asian American diversity and culture!
elections: Elections will occur at the last general meeting of each semester. Generally each cabinet position has a year-long term, however if a cabinet member is graduating or under other circumstances there will be an election at the end of the Fall semester to fill the position.
meetings: The first meeting of the 2025 - 2026 academic year will be on Friday, September 19th, at the SIC from 6:30 - 7:30! After that, we will have bi-weekly meetings every Thursday! Follow us on Instagram @asu_iastate for more info and updates!
activities: ASU meets bi-weekly to bring our members together for various events, from fun social events, professional events, cultural celebrations, and more! Our goal through these events is to build and foster a strong community at Iowa State University with Asian identity, culture, and appreciation as the foundation of our connection between members. We often also partner with Iowa State University's Vietnamese Student Association, fostering an even larger and strong community between Asian students and non-Asian students on campus!
specialEvents:
Midwest Asian American Students Union (MAASU) Conference —

each spring, ASU supports and encourages members to attend this weekend-long event. [maasu.org]

homeText:
Welcome to the Badminton Club at Iowa State University!

The Badminton Club at Iowa State University is open to players of all skill levels - Whether you’re here to smash, drop, rally, or just figure out which side of the racket to use.

We’re all about good rallies, good vibes, and building a community that plays hard and laughs harder.

What We’re About

Our club is dedicated to:

Promoting the sport of badminton on campus

Providing opportunities for recreational and competitive play

Building a welcoming community of badminton enthusiasts

Encouraging teamwork, sportsmanship, and personal growth

Why Join Us?

🏸 Weekly practices & open play

🤝 Meet fellow students who love badminton

🏆 Opportunities to compete in tournaments and events

💪 Stay active and relieve stress

😄 Zero pressure - play at your own pace

💸 Opportunity to be a part of the fundraising events

Who Can Join?

All Iowa State students are welcome! No prior experience required. Just bring comfortable athletic wear, a good attitude, and a willingness to have fun.

Practice Timings

Come play with us during our weekly sessions:

- Fridays: 7:00 PM – 9:30 PM

- Sundays: 3:00 PM – 7:00 PM

You don’t have to stay the entire time - drop in whenever you can! Feel free to hop in anytime.

name: Beta Alpha Psi
description:
Beta Alpha Psi is a National Accounting Honor Society described as the following:
"As the premier Accounting and business information fraternity, Beta Alpha Psi recognizes academic excellence and complements members' formal education by providing interaction between students, faculty, business professionals, and fosters lifelong growth, service and ethical conduct."

Beta Alpha Psi is an honorary organization for Accounting, Finance, and Management Information Systems (MIS) students and professionals. The primary objective of Beta Alpha Psi is to encourage and give recognition to scholastic and professional excellence in the business information field. This includes promoting the study and practice of accounting, finance, and information systems; providing opportunities for self-development, service and association among members and practicing professionals, and encouraging a sense of ethical, social, and public responsibility.

Beta Alpha Psi was founded in 1919. In 2006, there were 263 chapters on college and university campuses with over 300,000 members initiated since Beta Alpha Psi's formation. - Beta Alpha Psi National Office
membershipQualifications:
Must have completed 45 college credits with 1 upper level Accounting, Finance, or Information Systems course completed beyond the business core classes. Must have a cumulative grade point of 3.00. Have a minimum of 3.00 GPA.

Review member/pledge requirements.
membershipRestrictions: Must be an Accounting, Finance, Analytics, or Management Information Systems major.
allowedMembers: Students whom meet the requirements below.
elections: Each semester an election is held for executive board positions.
meetings: Every Tuesday and Thursday at 5:20pm from start of fall semester until Meet the Firms, then every Tuesday evening at 5:20pm until the end of the spring semester.
activities: Meetings with professional companies, such as KPMG, John Deere, HNI, Becker, and many more. These companies discuss tips on recruiting, resume-building, how to land a job/internship, and what a typical day on the job looks like for these companies. We also host community service projects, such as Project Linus and craft-building for children who have been hospitalized due to chronic illness.
specialEvents: Special events include tours of local companies, such as Workiva and ISU's Athletic center. We also host an event called "Platinum Sponsor" in which we have BAP members and our top-sponsored companies spend a fun evening bowling and mingling at Perfect Games. Our biggest event of the year is our pre-career fair event Meet the Firms, where companies come to ISU's campus to recruit for their open internship and full-time positions. At the end of every semester we host an end-of-the-semester banquet where we recognize our highly-participating members, graduating members, and initiated members.

name: Beta Theta Pi
description:
Beta Theta Pi is dedicated to building men of principle for a principled life. Our brotherhood aids the individual, builds the Fraternity, and strengthens the host academic institution through lifelong devotion to intellectual excellence, high standards of moral conduct, and responsible citizenship.

The Tau Sigma chapter of Beta Theta Pi was started at Iowa State in 1905, before closing in 2005 and reopening in fall 2006. We are already an award-winning chapter, distinguished among Beta chapters internationally for campus involvement, leadership development, and excellence in risk management. We are always geared towards progress in what we consider the rebuilding of our great tradition at Iowa State. We are always looking for men who would like to make their mark at Iowa State and positively contribute to the Sorority and Fraternity Community, campus, and Ames. We are gentlemen, scholars, and leaders.

name: Birding Club
description: Birding Club provides students with an opportunity to bond over a common interest in birds, their conservation, and in nature as a whole. The meetings include various bird-related presentations, games, or videos and the environment is very casual. membershipQualifications: None
elections: November
meetings: Every Tuesday from 6-7 pm in Science II, room 202.
activities: Each general meeting will last no longer than sixty minutes. Meetings will consist of: member presentations, a guest speaker, or birding activities/games (i.e. birding jeopardy, kahoot, trivia, etc.). Every other week, the club will go on local field trips to practice birding, observe annual migrations, participate in avian conservation, or engage in birding competitions with other university birding clubs. specialEvents: Each semester, the club will go on 1-2 weekend field trips out of state. Additionally, the club will also go to the annual spring Prairie Chicken breeding grounds in southern Iowa.

name: BOOST: Sports Engineering Club
description: BOOST (Building Optimized Outcomes in Sports Technology) is a sports engineering club at Iowa State University. The club dives into a variety of sports with scientific and problem-solving mindsets, to study past engineering marvels in sports, as well as creating new technology to be used in sports. Analyzing sports technologies using slideshows/videos

Building new sports technologies

Building budget sports technologies for donation

Guest speakers from current sporting goods companies

name: Boxing Club
description:
The Boxing Club welcomes all students interested in learning and experiencing the sport of boxing, whether your goal is stress relief, fitness, building routine during academic life, or pursuing competition. We are a USA Boxing–registered gym with certified coaches and a strong commitment to safety.

Our members train in an environment that balances discipline with camaraderie. We host annual events, travel to amateur and collegiate gyms for sparring and competition, and grow together through hard work, laughter, and community.

The club emphasizes breaking down common stereotypes about boxing by promoting respect, sportsmanship, and inclusivity. Above all, we strive to be a “home away from home,” creating a family-style atmosphere where every member is supported, challenged, and encouraged to reach their full potential both inside and outside the ring.

homeText:
The Boxing Club welcomes all students interested in learning and experiencing the sport of boxing, whether your goal is stress relief, fitness, building routine during academic life, or pursuing competition. We are a USA Boxing–registered gym with certified coaches and a strong commitment to safety.

Our members train in an environment that balances discipline with camaraderie. We host annual events, travel to amateur and collegiate gyms for sparring and competition, and grow together through hard work, laughter, and community.

The club emphasizes breaking down common stereotypes about boxing by promoting respect, sportsmanship, and inclusivity. Above all, we strive to be a “home away from home,” creating a family-style atmosphere where every member is supported, challenged, and encouraged to reach their full potential both inside and outside the ring.

*If you do NOT have prior experience, you are required to participate in the fundamentals boot camp offered each semester (see 2026 Fundamentals Boot Camp for more information).

**If you DO have prior experience, please see Prior Experience (below) to determine if you are eligible to bypass the fundamentals boot camp.

Club Practice Times:​

- Monday, and Wednesday @ 6:30-7:45 PM (technique/skill development)

- Tuesday @ 6:30-7:30 PM (mitt work/partner drills)

- Thursday @ 6:30-7:30 PM (pre-programmed 'solo' workout)

- Friday @ 6:30-8:30 PM (sparring and open gym)

Club Practice Location: Basement of State Gym.

*2025/2026 Fundamentals Boot Camp:

- Mondays and Wednesdays @ 5:15-6:15 PM (see Club Practice Location)

- FALL (2026) BOOT CAMP TIMES: SEPTEMBER 14 - OCTOBER 28

**Prior Experience: Our coaching staff considers individuals eligible to bypass the fundamentals class if they meet one of the following criteria: they have trained at a USA Boxing registered gym (or a comparable international facility) for more than three months; they have sparring or competition experience as a registered USA Boxing athlete in a USA Boxing gym (or comparable international facility); or they have over six months of training in a gym or military facility that emphasizes combat sports with a focus on striking.

Governing Body: USA Boxing (all athlete and non-athlete members are registered through USA Boxing; all non-athlete members have a minimum of a green-level coaching certification and are SafeSport certified).

LBC Affiliate: USIBA (United States Intercollegiate Boxing Association).

- Club: $50

name: Cardinal Space Mining Club
description: Cardinal Space Mining Club is a group of students in, but not limited to, the fields of science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM). The group will annually design and build a robotic mining system to compete in the NASA Robotic Mining Competition. As a result, the members of the Cardinal Space Mining Club will be challenged to create an atmosphere of community and excitement among students, learning from and teaching other students, welcoming prospective students and community members, connecting students with faculty and community through projects, activities, and demonstrations.
membershipQualifications: Need to be a full-time student at Iowa State University with a cumulative GPA of at least 2.0.
membershipRestrictions: All majors are encouraged to join Cardinal Space Mining Club by paying the dues.
elections: Elections take place in April and the date is decided a month prior to the election month. Any dues-paying member is eligible to run for a position.
meetings: Our General Meeting is on Thursdays at 6:00 PM in the SIC, and the Workday is on Saturday at 10:00 AM in the SIC, the exact rooms are subject to change.
activities:
General Meetings are Thursdays at 6:00 pm in the SIC. They are the best place to find out more about the club and the plans for the upcoming week.

Cardinal Space Mining Club is divided into three subteams: Controls, Mechanical, and Systems.

The Controls team focuses on the electronics and software aspects of the robot, including LIDAR vision and autonomy.

The Mechanical team designs and manufactures the robot, including CAD, machining, and assembly.

The Systems team is in charge of ensuring that the team stays on track, and explaining our engineering process to judges.

Additionally, an Outreach Lead coordinates events aimed at recruiting new members or spreading knowledge of STEM to our community.

These teams meet additionally outside the general meeting with time and location varying from team to team.
specialEvents:
NASA’s annual Lunabotics Competition is a competition for students to design and build a robot that competes in a simulated lunar environment to mine regolith.

Cardinal Space Mining Club participates in NASA's Lunabotics Competition every May at the Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida.

name: Central Asian Student Association
description:
Central Asian Student Association at Iowa State University is a culture- and identity-based student organization dedicated to building a supportive community for students from Central Asia and those interested in the region. The organization promotes cultural awareness, inclusion, and cross-cultural understanding by celebrating the histories, traditions, and shared experiences of Central Asian countries, including Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan.

The association provides a welcoming space for students to connect, share their culture, and support one another academically and socially. Through cultural programming, educational initiatives, and collaboration with other student organizations, the group aims to increase visibility of Central Asian cultures on campus and contribute to a more inclusive university community.
elections: Officer elections are held once per academic year during the spring semester, typically in April, to select leadership for the following academic year. Elections are conducted during a general body meeting and are open to active members in good standing. If a position becomes vacant during the year, a special election or appointment may be held to ensure continuity of leadership.
meetings: General body meetings are held bi-weekly during the fall and spring semesters. Meetings take place in person on campus, with the option for virtual attendance when necessary. Meetings focus on organizational updates, event planning, cultural discussions, and community-building activities. Additional meetings may be scheduled as needed for officers or committees.
activities: The Central Asian Student Association holds bi-weekly general body meetings during the fall and spring semesters. Meetings are typically held in person on campus, with a virtual option available when needed. Meetings focus on community building, cultural discussions, planning upcoming events, and supporting members academically and socially. Additional officer or committee meetings may be scheduled as needed.

name: Classics Club/ Eta Sigma Phi
description:
Eta Sigma Phi is an honorary organization for outstanding students in Latin and Greek language courses at Iowa State.
The Classics Club is a subcommittee of Eta Sigma Phi at Iowa State that is also devoted to the culture of the Classical world (including Greece, Rome, and Egypt), literature, history, etc. but has less strict requirements for membership.
membershipQualifications:
Interest in classics (Greece and Rome), is required. You do not have to be a Classical Studies minor or major. In order to be a member, just contact one of the officers and let us know you are interested! In order to be an officer, you must have a cumulative GPA of 2.00.
We are a subcommittee of the Iowa State Chapter of Eta Sigma Phi. In order to join Eta Sigma Phi, you must have completed two semesters of Latin and have a minimum GPA of 3.50. However, you do not need to be in Eta Sigma Phi in order to be a part of Classics Club.
membershipRestrictions: No restrictions, just interest in classics!
elections: We will hold elections at the end of each school year during our last club meeting.
meetings: Every other Thursday starting January 31st, 2019.
activities: We meet every other Wednesday in Pearson 3131 at 6 P.M. We hold a variety of events, from history/mythology presentations from our club members to mock archaeological digs.
specialEvents: Our special events will be mass emailed to everyone on our email list. Our special events include potential visits to Classical related museums in the Midwest or a movie night with a Classical themed movie.

name: CMAA Future
description: CMAA Future is a collegiate organization dedicated to fostering the professional development of students interested in private club management and the broader hospitality industry. Affiliated with the national CMAA, the student chapter provides opportunities for members to gain hands-on experience, network with industry leaders, and enhance their understanding of club operations.
elections: Candidates for officer positions are typically required to be active student members of both the local student chapter and the national CMAA organization. It is often recommended that elected officers be second- to fourth-year students or graduate students to ensure familiarity with chapter operations and institutional procedures. A Nomination Committee will be appointed annually to oversee the nomination and election of officers.
meetings: CMAA Future typically holds meetings on a regular basis, though the frequency may vary depending on the chapter's size, goals, and university policies. The general member meetings will be held monthly. These meetings provide updates on upcoming events, guest speakers, networking opportunities, and industry trends.
activities: The general member meetings provide updates on upcoming events, guest speakers, networking opportunities, and industry trends. They may also include educational sessions, discussions, or career development workshops. The chapter’s officers (President, Vice President, Treasurer, Secretary, etc.) meet more frequently to discuss chapter operations, event planning, and strategic initiatives. Additionally, industry professionals, club managers, and CMAA representatives may be invited for guest lectures, panel discussions, and networking sessions. These events typically take place a few times per semester.
specialEvents: Our major event of the year is usually attending the CMAA World Conference. In 2020 it will be in Dallas, TX, February 8-12. Students participate in a number of activities, including networking with other school chapters, attending seminars with industry leaders, and interviewing for jobs and internships. We also meet with our parent chapter of CMAA, the Tall Corn Chapter, regularly.

name: Cognitive Area Psychology Students (CAPS)
description: The primary purpose of this organization is to enhance the research experience and professional development of graduate students in the Cognitive Psychology graduate program at ISU.
elections:
This organization designates the following official positions up for annual elections: President, Vice President, and Treasurer. Election of officers will be held during the month of April using a secret ballot and will require a simple majority vote from the general membership. If a candidate fails to receive a simple majority of votes, a run-off election will be held between the two top candidates that received the most votes. This run-off election will occur within one week of the previous vote.

All candidates must be nominated for candidacy either by another member or by her or himself. Additionally, the candidate must accept this nomination either in person or in writing to the presiding president within 24 hours of said nomination in order to be placed on the ballot.
meetings: The organization will hold regular meetings during the academic year. The president is obligated to inform the general membership within the first three weeks of each semester when these meetings will occur.
activities: CAPS will hold at least one all-member meeting during each Fall and Spring semester. The meeting dates will be set according to the members’ availability as determined by a poll of active members at the beginning of each semester. In this meeting, we shall discuss potential events and speakers with the general membership. Additional all-member meetings will be held if needed to discuss important departmental or organizational updates.
specialEvents: CAPS will host one or two talks from outside speakers per year (as long as funding permits). These speakers will give either a research talk related to cognitive psychology or will provide non-academic expertise relevant to Cognitive Psychology students. These events will be planned by the CAPS executive board.

name: College Democrats
description:
The College Democrats are a direct route for our fellow students to engage with politics. We instill values of environmental, racial, and economic justice, encourage young people to participate in the American political process, and provide opportunities to work on Democratic campaigns. We also serve as a place to discuss current events, vent about politics, and meet some like-minded people!

Whether it’s meeting with local politicians, tabling outside of the library, volunteering in the community, or door-knocking in the dead of winter (donuts included) we always have a good time! The College Democrats is an official chapter of the College and Young Democrats of Iowa, which itself is co-chartered through College Democrats of America and Young Democrats of America.

activities: Join our email list/follow our socials to get exact meeting details!
specialEvents: We host informative events with candidates, special issue events, and demonstrations. The best way to stay updated about our special events is to join our email list. We also keep our social media pages updated with our events. Check us out at @dems.isu!

name: College of Veterinary Medicine Association of Graduate Students
description: We are the graduate student organization that serves the College of Veterinary Medicine. The CVMAGS has several different departments and we recognize that there is no such organization which brings together all students from these departments. We aim to provide a place where all students of CVM can intermingle, exchange ideas, network, and express their concerns that relate to not just their departments, but to CVM as a whole. We also participate in various outreach and volunteer events each throughout the year in the Ames area.
membershipQualifications: Membership shall be open to all registered graduate students in good standing at Iowa State University’s College of Veterinary Medicine.
membershipRestrictions: Members who are not in good standing will be asked to remove themselves from the associate and focus on their academic standing before returning to the association.
allowedMembers: Graduate students based in the College of Veterinary Medicine
elections:
All constituents of the CVMAGS shall have one eligible vote in CVMAGS elections.
Elections shall be held by secret ballot and 75% of active members must be present and voting.
Elections shall be held in April.
The Commissioner of Elections shall certify the results of all elections on or before the Thursday preceding the second-to-last Friday of April.
meetings:
At least one (1) regular meeting will be held each month from September to May, while the CVM is in session.
Within the first week of classes beginning, the President will publically announce the date/time/location of each regular meeting for the semester to all of the constituents and include the future methods of communication for the CVMAGS including, but not limited to, email lists and websites.
Included in the last regular meeting in May, following the accession to office by new officers, the elected officers shall establish a schedule specifying the time/date/location for each regular meeting for the following academic year.
Requests for special meeting will be called by the President if a written demand is submitted by/including 1/3 of active members
The Secretary shall send each member written notice of all regular and special meetings at least seven (7) days prior to such meetings. Ex. email, campus mail, U.S. mail all acceptable.
activities: One meeting is held each month from September to May. These are usually held on Tuesdays during lunch.

We also participate in various outreach and volunteer events each throughout the year in the Ames area.

name: College of Veterinary Medicine Class of 2027
description: The purpose of "The College of Veterinary Medicine Class of 2027" shall be to govern the Iowa State University College of Veterinary Medicine Class of 2027. Our goals include, but are not limited to, functioning as a liaison between the Iowa State University College of Veterinary Medicine administration and “The College of Veterinary Medicine Class of 2027,” facilitation of social activities among members, academic support in the form of organizing review sessions and moving exams, funding and planning of “The College of Veterinary Medicine Class of 2027” graduation banquet, and lastly, a class gift to the Iowa State University College of Veterinary Medicine.
elections: The term of office will be one academic year for President, Vice President, Secretary, and Treasurer. A month prior to finals week of each Spring semester of the academic year, the Executive Board should poll the club on the decision for retaining current Officers or electing new Officers through simple majority vote. If a vote shall be held, it should be no later than three weeks prior to finals week. If new Officer(s) are elected, they will work with the current Officer(s) in the last few weeks of the semester to transfer any relative documents and training to the incoming Officer(s). Relinquishment of Officer duties will occur after the last day of finals of that Spring semester. Instatement of the new Officer(s) will occur on the same day in which the outgoing Officer(s) relinquish their duties. All Officers and Advisors shall comprise the Executive Board of the organization. The Executive Board shall meet in addition to regular organization meetings. The Executive Board shall appoint such committees that are needed to carry out organization goals.
meetings: All Officers and Advisors shall comprise the Executive Board of the organization. The Executive Board shall meet in addition to regular organization meetings. Service is Key

An integral part of the mission of Collegiate 4-H is to serve the community around us. This is done through monthly service projects which are selected by club members. These vary throughout the year to include everything from helping with Food at First to making blankets YSS (Youth Shelter Services).

Fun With Business

Members have the opportunity to attend monthly business meetings that also allow time for service projects and fun activities. We try to have at least one informational speaker at each meeting and welcome professional development activities. During this time members have a chance to help make key decisions within the club.

Moving Forward

Collegiate 4-H strives to create a space where our members are able to develop professional connections and hone leadership skills. The club offers chances for members to attend national and regional conferences, meet with many state 4-H extension employees, and serve in numerous leadership roles.

Open Door

We welcome anyone to become a member regardless of whether they have been a 4-H'er before. Whether you're a freshman or senior, we welcome you to come visit us at one of our meetings!

homeText:
About Us

Computer Science and Software Engineering Club (CSE for short) is ISU's primary club for anything programming related. Our goal is to create a friendly, educational, and engaging environment for anyone interested in computer science/software development. We offer a variety of events ranging from presentations from industry-leading companies to fun and relaxed games nights. No programming experience is required, all majors are welcome, and there is no fee to join. All you need is an interest in programming/development!

What We Do

CSE Club offers a variety of events to our members, all of which are completely free. We have weekly meetings (days and times below) that feature company presentations, educational workshops, or game nights. All of our meetings offer opportunities to network with other students or industry professionals. Aside from our weekly club meetings, we also look to host events with other computer science clubs like the Robotics Club and Game Development Club. Lastly, we are also looking to create a variety of "interest groups" within the club that focus on a specific areas of computer science/software development such as Cloud Technologies, CI/CD, and Python Development to name a few (details below).

How To Get Involved

The first step to joining the club is to request to join via StuOrg using the link at the top-right of this page. You will receive a confirmation email when your request has been accepted and will be enrolled in emails about club activities. However, the best way to stay up-to-date on club activities and meet other members is to join our Discord using this link: https://discord.gg/retmDM8yfw

Meeting Info

Weekly meetings are held every Monday from 6:00pm-7:00pm in Carver 0268. Meeting details are posted in Discord and sent via email a few days prior to the meeting and a regularly updated agenda is posted in the Discord.

Interest Groups

In an effort to promote communication amongst club members and engage more member's interest's directly, we are looking to create "interest groups" within the club. Each interest group has a single focus, such as Python development, and a chairperson to lead help manage the group's activities and coordinate with the rest of the club. If you are interested in creating a new interest group, please reach out to the current president or vice-president via Discord or email!

elections:
Election Procedures
Annual election of officers shall be scheduled midterm during a regular Culinary Science Club meeting during the Fall term (Election Meeting).

Nominations
The Nomination Meeting will occur one General Business Meeting prior to the Election Meeting, ONLY those members who are present may be nominated. The nominees will be asked to Accept or Decline the nomination. Self-Nominations ONLY may be emailed to the President up to 2 weeks before the Election Meeting.

Voting
Only active dues-paying members may participate in elections. It is the duty of the Treasurer to determine if the member is eligible to vote.
Voting will be done via secret ballot. Members will write the name of the candidate they wish to vote for on the paper. Ballots will be counted for each office, one at a time, beginning with the office of President. After ballots are counted for that office, the winner is announced and the process continues through the remaining positions.

The Hare System of Vote Counting
Election Meeting:
All Nominees shall have a brief opportunity to express interest in the Executive position they have been nominated for prior to the vote. All nominated members must leave the meeting while each nominee is presenting and while ballots are being counted.
Nominations shall be called and election held for one office at a time, beginning with the office of the President. Candidates not elected to one office shall be eligible for nomination to succeeding offices, ONLY if the nominee is present.
A majority of all votes cast shall be necessary for election. If there are three or more candidates for one office, and no candidate receives a majority vote on the first ballot, the candidate receiving the least votes shall be eliminated, and balloting shall continue in the same manner for the remaining candidates until one shall have received a majority. Tie votes for any office shall be resolved by lot, by the President.

Election Results
As soon as the written ballots are completed, 2 members of the Executive Committee will count the votes. The faculty advisor will observe the counting to ensure no errors are made. The officers-elect will be announced during the meeting.

name: Cyber Robotics
description:
Cyber Robotics fosters an innovative and inclusive environment where students can explore and enrich their skills in robotics, engineering, problem-solving, and logistics through participation in VEX U Robotics Competition. Our club aims to provide opportunities for members to develop and expand soft skills in professional communication, strategic thinking, and leadership. Engaging in hands-on projects with collaborative interdisciplinary engineering, expanding STEM education outside the classroom, and representing Iowa State University at competitions are core objectives of the Cyber Robotics.

Every year, we are given a new challenge for which we design, manufacture, program, and document multiple robots to compete against other collegiate teams across the world at regional and international competitions.

name: Dance Marathon
description:
Dance Marathon is Iowa State University’s largest student-run philanthropic organization. This organization raises funds and awareness year-round for the University of Iowa Stead Family Children’s Hospital over in Iowa City.

They also support approximately 32 local families who have been impacted by childhood illness and treated at the University of Iowa Stead Family Children’s Hospital. They host events year-round for these families so that kids can be kids. This year, Dance Marathon at ISU is raising funds for the Stead Family Children’s Hospital's brand new Wags and Waves Facility Dog Program which helps kiddos cope and heal during their hospital visits.

Beyond the impact on local kiddos and their families, this organization works to foster a community of leaders on Iowa State’s campus through various leadership and development opportunities. Functioning similarly to a non-profit business, Dance Marathon can offer valuable experience that directly relates to many colleges and their majors.

Each year, Dance Marathon celebrates all of their hard work at the Big Event. The Big Event takes place at the Iowa State Memorial Union during the second weekend in February and it is a day dedicated to the families they support. With engaging activities throughout the day, Dance Marathon reminds everyone the joys of just being a kid. At the end of the event, Dance Marathon does a tote board flip on stage that reveals the total amount of money they raised for the University of Iowa Stead Family Children’s Hospital.
membershipQualifications: Looking for leadership experience and other campus involvement.
membershipRestrictions: Must be a current undergraduate or graduate student at Iowa State University.
elections: Applications for Iowa State Dance Marathon Executive Committee are released each February following Dance Marathon. General Committee applications are released each March with an interview processes following application deadlines.
meetings: Meetings are held biweekly with each individual committee and monthly with all of Dance Marathon leadership.
activities: Committee members meet weekly to plan and facilitate Dance Marathon events specific to their committee. All-committee meetings are held monthly.
associations: Miracle Network Dance Marathon: a program of Children's Miracle Network Hospital
homeText:
Dance Marathon at Iowa State University is the largest student-run philanthropic organization on campus. We hold many events throughout the year to raise funds and awareness for the families impacted by treatment at the University of Iowa Health Care Stead Family Children's Hospital, located in Iowa City. Every spring, we celebrate our hard work and create a fun atmosphere for students and families at our Big Event!

University of Iowa Health Care Stead Family Children's Hospital is Iowa's only comprehensive children's hospital and the only nationally ranked children's hospital in Iowa. Each year, UI Stead serves over 100,000 children from all 99 counties in Iowa.

Dance Marathon is not a competition and requires no dancing abilities! We are a member of Children's Miracle Network Dance Marathon, a nationwide, student-led movement that empowers students to make a difference in their own communities by raising funds to change kids' health to change the future. During our annual big event celebration, there's a morale dance (an easy line dance) that participants have an opportunity to learn, but if dancing's not your thing, there are also games, inflatables, performers, food, and more! Plus, you get the opportunity to interact with and meet some of our amazing miracle families.

For more information about Dance Marathon visit our website at https://dm.stuorg.iastate.edu/

name: Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc. Phi Chapter
description:
Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc. is a non-profit organization whose purpose is to provide assistance and support through established programs in local communities throughout the world. A sisterhood of more than 200,000 predominately Black, college educated women, the Sorority currently has over 900 chapters located in the United States and abroad.

The Sorority was founded January 13, 1913 by 22 students at Howard University. These young women wanted to use their collective strength to promote academic excellence; to provide scholarships; to provide support to the underserved; educate and stimulate participation in the establishment of positive public policy; and to highlight issues and provide solutions for problems in their communities.

Phi Chapter was chartered December 29, 1923 in Des Moines, Iowa. It is a joint chapter between Iowa State University and Drake University. Phi Chapter has a long history of service to its campus communities. Some Phi Chapter programs include Highway Cleanup, Ladies Night Out, Chili and a Movie, and the Ames Martin Luther King Jr. Celebration.

activities:
General Assembly Meetings

Section 1 – Order of Business

A. All formal meetings of the Chapter shall be conducted in the following order;

1. Opening ceremonies

3. Introduction of visiting members

4. Executive committee reports

5. Committee chairmen reports

6. Old business

7. New business

8. Chapter member critiques

9. Suggestions for the good of the Order (passing the gavel)

10. Closing ceremonies

Section 2 – Meeting Procedure

A. The current edition of Robert’s Rules of Order will govern meetings, except where specified by

the bylaws of Gamma Pi chapter of Delta Tau Delta Fraternity.

B. The President of the Chapter shall chair all General Assembly meetings, or a member in good

standing in the Chapter, chosen by the Sergeant-at- Arms and whom the presiding officer at the

meeting approves of.

C. Profanity and outburst will not be tolerated.

Section 3– Time and Place

A. Regular meetings shall be held each Sunday evening at 6:30pm sharp, in the Chapter Hall at

2121 Sunset Drive, Ames, Iowa.

B. Active Member Education will take place every 3 rd Sunday of the month in place of the regular

chapter meetings, if deemed necessary by the Executive Committee. Attendance and a paper

chapter will occur at the beginning of this Sunday meeting.

homeText:
Design Council is a student-led advocacy group in the College of Design. We work in tandem with faculty and staff leadership to provide services to College of Design students. Most importantly, we work with the student body to advocate their voices and raise them to higher leadership with the goal of conducting real change.

Design Council operates with two main sectors. The first is our leadership positions, who attend faculty meetings and work alongside departments and offices (such as the Multicultural Student Success Office), members of College of Design student organizations, and other leadership roles. The second group consists of the general public. Everyone can attend our general meetings, and all events hosted or promoted by the Design Council are all inclusive.

The goal of Design Council is to create a stronger sense of community in the College of Design, to raise student voices, build connections with faculty leadership, and provide spaces for students to feel safe.

name: Ducks Unlimited
description:
Ducks Unlimited (DU) is the world’s largest private, nonprofit organization dedicated to conserving North America’s wetlands and waterfowl habitat. Founded in 1937 during the Dust Bowl, DU was created by a group of sportsmen who recognized the urgent need to protect declining waterfowl populations and the wetlands they depend on.

Today, Ducks Unlimited works across North America to protect, restore, enhance, and manage wetlands, grasslands, forests, and other critical habitats. Through partnerships with private landowners, government agencies, scientists, businesses, and volunteers, DU uses science-based conservation to improve habitat for ducks, geese, and hundreds of other wildlife species. These projects also provide benefits for people and communities by improving water quality, reducing flood risks, protecting watersheds, and preserving outdoor recreation opportunities.

Since its founding, DU and its partners have conserved more than 20 million acres of habitat across North America and completed more than 20,000 conservation projects. In fiscal year 2025 alone, DU delivered more than 1.2 million acres of conservation, marking its second consecutive year exceeding one million acres in a single year. In 2026, DU also completed its historic "Conservation for a Continent" campaign, raising $4.06 billion to support wetlands and waterfowl conservation - far exceeding its original $3 billion goal.

At its core, Ducks Unlimited is committed to ensuring that wetlands and waterfowl thrive for future generations, while preserving the hunting, fishing, and outdoor traditions that connect people to these landscapes.
